title: What is the balance after eight debits and one big credit?
description: An account starts with nothing in it. Eight debits of one, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty two, sixty four and one hundred and twenty eight rupees go out, and one credit of two hundred and fifty six rupees comes in. The debits are added and taken away from the credit.
teaching_notes: One idea: add all the debits first, then compare the total with the credit. Watch for students who count the entries instead of adding the amounts.

video_script.why: The child adds eight debits, takes the total away from one credit, and finds a small positive balance.
video_script.substitution: Add all the debits, then take the debit total away from the credit.
video_script.design: One passbook with eight small debits and one tall credit. The debits are added with running totals, then taken away from the credit. The check puts the balance and the debits back together to make the credit.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a bank passbook with an empty account; eight small debits 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 go out; one tall credit of 256 comes in; the words What is the balance now? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.start: an account with nothing in it is shown
marks.debits: eight small debits go out, each twice the one before
marks.credit: one tall credit of 256 comes in
marks.ask: the question appears under the passbook

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, about a bank account.
<bookmark mark='start'/>The account starts with nothing in it.
<bookmark mark='debits'/>Eight small debits go out, and each is twice the one before.
<bookmark mark='credit'/>Then one credit of two hundred and fifty six rupees comes in.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the balance now?

beats.on_screen: the passbook and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a short red block for each small debit beside one tall green block for the credit; the size of each amount matters

marks.debits: eight short red blocks stand in a row
marks.credit: one tall green block stands beside them
marks.size: the blocks are compared by their size and not by how many there are

narration: <bookmark mark='debits'/>Each small debit takes the balance down a little.
<bookmark mark='credit'/>One tall credit can bring the balance up by a lot.
<bookmark mark='size'/>The size of each amount matters, and not how many there are.

marks.small: the first five debits are written in a row
marks.last: the last three debits are written in a row
marks.credit: the credit is written in its own row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the account starts with nothing.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The first debits are one, two, four, eight and sixteen rupees.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last three are thirty two, sixty four and one hundred and twenty eight rupees.
<bookmark mark='credit'/>The credit is two hundred and fifty six rupees.

marks.find: the words the balance now are written and underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the balance in the account now.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: add the debits one at a time. Running totals: 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255

marks.run: the debits are added one at a time and the running total is written under each
marks.total: the debit total 255 is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='run'/>Step one, add the debits one at a time. The running total goes one, three, seven, fifteen, thirty one, sixty three, and one hundred and twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The last debit makes the total two hundred and fifty five rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: take the debits away from the credit, 256 − 255; the tall credit is taller than all eight debits together

marks.take: the debit total of 255 is taken away from the credit of 256
marks.left: one small block of the credit stays above the empty line

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step two, take the debit total away from the credit.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The credit is bigger than all eight debits together, so a little money stays in the account.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, check: the balance and the debits must make the credit, 1 + 255 = 256

marks.back: the balance 1 and the debits 255 are put together
marks.again: they make the credit of 256 again

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, check by adding the balance back to the debits.
<bookmark mark='again'/>One and two hundred and fifty five make two hundred and fifty six, which is the credit.

marks.ans: the balance (256 − 255 = +1) is written and boxed as ₹1

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The balance is one rupee.
